paper.title: Unprecedented combination of specific tensile strength and ductility achieved in a novel duplex low-density steel
paper.paper_scope: Develops a novel Fe-Mn-Al-C-Cr austenite-ferrite duplex low-density steel (30Mn-13Al-1.3C-5Cr) by annealing a cold-rolled sheet at 600–1050 °C for 1–5 min, and studies how annealing temperature/time governs the duplex microstructure (recrystallized austenite, granular α ferrite, δ ferrite bands, κ-carbides and Cr7C3 carbides) and the resulting strength-ductility-density synergy (1250 MPa UTS, 41.4% TE at 6.36 g/cm3).

alloys.description: Novel lightweight Fe-Mn-Al-C-Cr steel created by redesigning the previous ultralow-density 29.05Mn-12.01Al-1.48C-5.13Cr austenitic steel into an austenite-ferrite duplex microstructure to further raise specific strength while keeping low density and large ductility. Melted in a vacuum induction furnace under argon, cast into ingot, forged to thick slab and hot rolled; about 5% Cr added to suppress intergranular κ-carbide formation; measured ultralow density of 6.36 g/cm3 (buoyancy balance, Archimedes principle).
alloys.alloys_notes: Weight percentage unless mentioned elsewhere. The abstract quotes the rounded composition 30Mn-13Al-1.3C-5Cr, while the main text gives the precise chemical composition 30.35Mn-12.60Al-1.32C-4.83Cr. About 5% Cr is added to suppress intergranular κ-carbides (refs 22,23). Measured ultralow density 6.36 g/cm3 by buoyancy balance according to Archimedes Principle.

source.reason: The abstract (b0009) and the main text composition section (b0012) describe a single redesigned austenite-ferrite duplex low-density steel of composition 30Mn-13Al-1.3C-5Cr / 30.35Mn-12.60Al-1.32C-4.83Cr; b0011 explains it is a redesign of the previous 29.05Mn-12.01Al-1.48C-5.13Cr austenitic steel. This is the only material system studied in the paper, so one alloy entity is defined.

unmapped_findings: The abstract states the study annealed a cold rolled 30Mn-13Al-1.3C-5Cr steel at 1000 °C to obtain tensile strength 1250 MPa, total elongation 41.4% and measured ultralow density 6.36 g/cm3 (b0009).

Two literature steels are used only as comparison benchmarks and were NOT experimentally studied in this work: the previous record austenitic steel 29.05Mn-12.01Al-1.48C-5.13Cr (Moon et al., SUTS 169.9 MPa·g-1·cm3, TE 43.8%, density 6.34 g/cm3) in b0010/b0011, and the 12Mn-5.5Al-0.7C duplex steel (Sohn et al., density 7.20 g/cm3) in b0011.

Tensile testing conditions: flat dog-bone specimens with 25 mm gage length, uniaxial tension at a strain rate of 10^-3 s^-1 at room temperature, three measurements per heat-treatment condition averaged (b0014).
Density of 6.36 g/cm3 measured by buoyancy balance according to Archimedes Principle (b0012).
Characterization techniques used: XRD, SEM (ZEISS Gemini 300), TEM (FEI Tecnai G20), EBSD (Scanning Auger Nanoprobe, PHI 710), and nanoindentation (b0014).
